partners.mechanism_chain: RAC2 (HGNC:9786) —DISRUPTS→ Neutrophil function (GO:0007650); Neutrophil function (GO:0007650) —LEADS_TO→ Neutrophil immunodeficiency syndrome (MONDO:0011988); APC (HGNC:555) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-169200); CTNNB1 (HGNC:2515) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-169200); Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-169200) —LEADS_TO→ Colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575). Loss-of-function mutations in RAC2 disrupt normal neutrophil function, leading to neutrophil immunodeficiency syndrome. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in APC and CTNNB1 disrupt the Wnt signaling pathway, a critical regulator of cell proliferation and differentiation, leading to the development of colorectal cancer. The Wnt signaling pathway, while not directly linked to RAC2's primary role in neutrophils, is a central pathway in cellular regulation that can be affected by mutations leading to cancer. Therefore, the overlap lies in the disruption of distinct but critical cellular regulatory pathways that, when dysregulated, manifest as distinct diseases.
